newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tyre venture draws Japan's Mitsui.
newsitem.headline: Indian tyre venture draws Japan's Mitsui.

text.p: Japanese trading giant Mitsui and Co Ltd said on Wednesday it had taken a 10 percent stake in Bridgestone ACC India Ltd, a joint tyre-making venture between Japan's Bridgestone Corp and India's Associated Cement Companies Ltd.(ACC)
"We have taken a 10 percent stake in Bridgestone ACC," a senior Mitsui official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters by telephone in the Indian capital.
Officials at ACC confirmed the Mitsui stake, and said Bridgestone's stake in the venture would rise to 64 percent from 51 percent.
A joint stake of ACC and Tata Engineering Locomotive Co will fall to 26 percent from 49 percent.
Bridgestone and ACC announced a 51-49 percent joint venture, Bridgestone ACC India ltd, in January 1996 to produce 2 million steel-belted passenger car radials a year in India.
ACC officials said the total project cost was 3.45 billion rupees ($96 million), with an equity capital of 1.39 billion rupees.
They said the tyre plant was being set up at Khera in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, and the first Bridgestone tyre was expected to be produced in April 1998.

India's fast expanding car market has become a big draw for global tyre companies. The Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers said car production stood at 404,040 vehicles in 1996/97 (April-March) and was expected to top a million vehicles by 2000.
Bridgestone will enter a vibrant tyre market dominated by local players such as Apollo Tyres Ltd, MRF Ltd and Ceat Ltd, and in which foreign companies have struggled to make a mark.
Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co's India unit, Goodyear India Ltd, has struggled for years to make its presence felt in the domestic market, but continues to remain out of the top five.
Germany's Continental AG has examined various ventures over the last several years, but has chosen to remain out of India.
France's Compagnie Generale Des Etablissements Michelin was forced to sell its stake in MRF Ltd by the management of the Indian company several years ago.

The Automotive Tyre Manufacturers' Association said India's tyre output grew to 27.89 million tyres in 1995/96 (April-March) from 19.95 million in 1992/93. In the first 10 months of 1996/97, production had crossed 27 million tyres.
